It is a shikinaisha and was formerly ranked as a prefectural shrine. {{nihongo|'''Hirose Shrine'''|広瀬神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
; Main deity
* Waka-Uka-no-Me-no-Mikoto

; Co-enshrined
* Kami-Hono-Musubi-no-Mikoto
* Konohana-Sakuya-Hime-no-Mikoto
* Yachimata-Hiko-no-Mikoto
* Yachimata-Hime-no-Mikoto
* Kunado-no-Mikoto

The first two correspond to deities of {{ill|Hirose Taisha|Q705281|qid=Q705281}} in Yamato. Additional deities were incorporated at shrine mergers in 1907.

== History ==
Shrine tradition says {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258}} enshrined deities here during his eastern campaign, comparing the landscape to Kawai in Yamato (site of Hirose Taisha). Modern scholarship sees the shrine name "Hirose" as likely a local topographic name (wide shallows at river confluence), not necessarily proof of direct branch origin from Yamato.

It is nonetheless an old influential shrine in Iruma District; in 850 it was listed as an official shrine in the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku,'' and in 927 it appears in the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho.''

In the Edo period, Hozoji (now extinct) served as betto temple. In 1823, old records were lost in a temple fire.

In 1873 it was made a gosha, then promoted to prefectural shrine in 1874 after local petition efforts by Shimizu Sotoku. At that time a school for training shrine clergy was also established in the precinct.

In 1907, Atago and Sengen shrines were merged into it. In 1909, the honden was moved to the center of the grounds and a new haiden built. Current structures were repaired/rebuilt in 1975.

== Precinct ==
* Subsidiary shrines: Inari Shrine, Hachiman Daijin Shrine, Kasumi Shrine (for local war dead)
* Two giant zelkova trees (former count was three): about 800 years old, around 30 m high, over 6 m trunk girth; designated Saitama natural monument
* Monument praising Shimizu Sotoku (erected 1914)

There are no komainu in the precinct; a local tradition says the main deity is female and dislikes rough symbols.

== Treasures ==
* Hanging Buddhist-style votive image donated by Hirose parishioners
* Imperial calligraphy attributed to Emperor Suko
* Inscribed swords (including one signed Bizen Osafune Sukesada)
